deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudo-lines, i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane or Möbius band, in the sense of Levi, Ringel, Grünbaum and Goodman-Pollack. The facing page counts N, the number of 'green' vertices (vertices of order 4) of a system F. It compares N with N' for a modified system F', finding N' = N-1 or N' = N. So this page is an attempt to define a surgery F -> F' that serves an inductive argument on the number of vertices.

The pictures. Red curves D1 and D2 are pseudolines crossing at a vertex s. Dark green is a pseudoline that bumps up to pass through s, with a dashed parallel copy. Light green is a straight pseudoline with a dashed parallel copy. Hatching marks the sides of strips. The strips are Δ_D, a band attached to the light-green line D, and Δ_{D'}, a band attached to the dark-green line D'. Grey arrows indicate the move: remove a band and glue (recoller) the dashed boundary of one strip onto the dashed boundary of the other. Each red line's segment D_i ∩ Δ_{D'} is then replaced by D_i ∩ Δ_D, and vice versa. In effect this is a cut-and-paste exchange of two parallel strips in the plane.

First configuration (top left): the vertex s lies in the excised region, so Grothendieck writes 'non ! (le sommet s disparaîtrait !)'. He adds that it is nevertheless worth seeing what that would give.

Second configuration (middle left): the strips are placed so that s is kept. The pieces D_i ∩ Δ_D continue unambiguously into D_i' ∩ Δ_{D'}, so the red lines are re-connected without ambiguity. However, he cannot track the 'circuits autour d'un trou' (loops around a hole) where the regluing takes place. This is a global, monodromy-type question: after gluing, does a red curve close up into a single pseudoline (one-sided, nontrivial class in π1(P^2)), and is the result again an arrangement?

Right-hand sketches: two variants (bumped and flat green line) where s again disappears near the gluing loci.

Bottom: the projective plane as a disk with antipodal boundary identification. The green circle is the line at infinity. Two red pseudolines meet at antipodal boundary points, which are a single point of P^2, and a red × marks a point. A second, deformed disk shows the boundary after regluing near the two poles.

Overall: an exploratory, failed or incomplete attempt at a strip-exchange surgery reducing the vertex count of a pseudoline system.
errors: No outright mathematical error. Grothendieck himself rejects the first configuration because it destroys the vertex s, and records an unresolved gap: the global consistency of the regluing ('circuits autour d'un trou') is not established. As stated, the surgery is not shown to produce a pseudoline system.

ideas.what: Cut-and-paste surgery on a pseudoline arrangement: excise a strip along one pseudoline and reglue, exchanging the traces D_i∩Δ_D and D_i∩Δ_{D'} of the other pseudolines.
ideas.modern_name: Local surgery/mutation of pseudoline arrangements (compare triangle flips, sweeps, deletion/contraction in oriented matroid rank 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flip-connectivity; Goodman-Pollack (1980s) for sweeping; oriented matroid theory (Folkman-Lawrence 1978, Björner et al.)
ideas.where_published: Pseudoline notes (cote 154) are unpublished; not in Esquisse or Récoltes et Semailles as such

ideas.what: Induction on the number N of order-4 vertices (simple crossings) via a move giving N' = N or N-1.
ideas.modern_name: Induction on crossings / vertex count in arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in combinatorial geometry (Grünbaum, Arrangements and Spreads, 1972)

ideas.what: Concern with monodromy of curves around holes created by regluing, i.e. checking that reglued arcs close up into one-sided pseudolines in P^2.

missed.claim: A proposed strip-exchange surgery for pseudoline systems, intended to lower the vertex count, is left unresolved because the global behaviour of curves around the gluing holes cannot be followed.
missed.quote: je n'arrive pas à suivre les "circuits autour d'un trou"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's hands-on combinatorial approach to pseudoline arrangements. The analogous reduction results (flip-connectivity, sweeping) are already well established in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: An exploratory sketch of a cut-and-paste move on pseudoline arrangements that Grothendieck himself flags as failing or incomplete. The underlying ideas are routine in combinatorial geometry, and there is no finished uncredited result.
transcription_corrections: The insertion after 'Et D_i∩Δ_{D'}' reads roughly '[struck word] ... par D_i∩Δ_D et vice-versa', i.e. D_i∩Δ_{D'} is replaced by D_i∩Δ_D and vice versa. The struck word is illegible (possibly 'disparaît' or 'remplacé').
'[Pourtant, ça vaut la peine de regarder ce que ça donnerait !)' is correct; the opening bracket is unmatched in the original.
'dans le cas [?] d'un trou où un recollement a lieu' is plausibly 'dans la cavité d'un trou où un recollement a lieu'; the reading is uncertain.
Bottom labels in the first figure: 'D_2' and 'D_1' are under the red lines (the second label may be a dagger-marked D_1). Bottom labels in the second figure are 'D_2'' and 'D_1''.
The bottom disk drawings (projective plane as a disk with antipodal identification, a red ×, and a deformed second disk) are not mentioned in the transcription.
